title: Establish temporal token scale and soft-shadow guidelines for compact interactive lists
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Motivation: current token scale and elevation prescriptions produce visual noise in dense lists (tables, compact lists, multi-row buttons). We need a cohesive set of tokens that: 1) scale temporally with interaction density (temporal token scale) so high-frequency interactive states remain legible without heavy elevation; 2) define a soft-shadow system that reads consistently across 90–1440px densities and reduces perceived depth while preserving affordance; 3) map to CSS/Android/iOS variables for an incremental rollout. This ticket covers token definitions, cross-platform naming, accessibility contrast checks, migration guidance for buttons, table rows, and chart overlays, and a staged rollout plan.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens defined: color ramp anchors, semantic surface levels (surface-0..surface-4), temporal type scale (compact/regular/relaxed) and radius presets (touch, compact, micro)
Soft-shadow recipes established with values for blur, spread, y-offset, and alpha that meet WCAG perceived contrast guidance for interactive affordances
Token names and CSS variable mapping documented and added to token source file in Figma + design tokens repo
Migration plan with automated codemods for core components (Button, TableRow, Card, ChartLegend) and a canary rollout strategy agreed
Cross-platform spec pages created for Web, iOS, Android with sample renderings at 3 densities
Design review approved by PM and Engineering and initial PR created that implements tokens in the dev sandbox
notes: Design trade-offs: prefer lowering elevation intensity and increasing subtle contrast of surface layers rather than introducing extra shadows for dense UIs — reduces GPU compositing overhead and visual clutter

Temporal token idea: tokens map to interaction-frequency buckets (micro, transient, persistent). E.g., micro-radius (4px) used for badges and compact rows; transient (6px) for buttons in dense lists; persistent (8–10px) for cards and modals
Accessibility: run automated contrast checks for foreground-on-surface at 14px and 16px in compact mode; ensure focus rings and keyboard targets remain >= 44px where possible

Implementation constraint: tokens must compile to existing token pipeline (JSON -> CSS vars -> platform SDKs). Work with ENG token pipeline owners to add new token keys and backwards-compatible aliases
Visual QA notes: test on 90 DPI laptop, 2x retina, and mobile small screens. Pay attention to chart overlays where faint shadows can reduce chart readability — provide 'overlay-flat' token for charts
Fallbacks: keep previous token aliases available for two releases (deprecation window) and include 'legacy-surface' mapping in codemods
Design files: included small set of examples for Buttons, Dense Table, Mini Chart Legend, and Mobile List Item (see design_files links)
qa_plan: Create visual regression tests for Button, Table row, and Card in compact and regular densities
Add unit tests that assert CSS var fallbacks for legacy mapping
Manual accessibility pass: keyboard navigation, focus visibility, color contrast at 14px/16px
Performance: measure compositing layers in Chromium Canary for dense lists before/after tokens applied
migration_steps: 1) Add new token JSON to tokens repo behind feature flag
2) Run codemod to replace legacy token keys in Button/Table/Chart components (script: tools/codemods/token-migrate.js)
3) Deploy UI library change to canary package (10% of routing) and monitor visual-regressions-dashboard and console token-heatmap
4) Notify integrators with migration guide and 'legacy-surface' fallback instructions
5) Remove legacy aliases in two releases after adoption metrics show <5% legacy usage
release_notes: Introduce temporal token scale and soft-shadow tokens to improve legibility in dense UIs. Includes migration tools and temporary legacy aliases. Default visual change limited to canary; full rollout after verification.
